title: Case Study 1: Fatal Fall from Height — Construction Site
learningObjectives: Apply the NEBOSH immediate–underlying–root cause framework to a real fall incident
Identify specific control failures that led to a fatal fall from height
Develop a prioritized corrective action plan with responsible parties and timelines
Understand how systemic failures compound to produce fatal injuries

content.text: This case describes a fatal workplace incident. All names and company details are fictional. Investigation findings are based on common patterns found in Gulf region construction fatalities reported to labour authorities.

During the construction of a commercial tower in Dubai, a scaffolding worker (Ahmed, 34) was installing formwork on Level 7 when he fell approximately 8 metres to the concrete slab below. He suffered fatal head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. The incident occurred at 14:00 on a weekday during peak summer heat.

Initial findings at the scene: the worker was not wearing a safety harness; a guardrail on the working platform edge had been removed by a previous crew and never reinstated; no supervisor was present at the work area at the time of the fall.

items: Activate emergency services (call 998 / site first aider)
Preserve the scene — cordon off Level 7 and the area below, allow no access
Do NOT move any equipment or materials until HSE investigation team arrives
Notify site management, main contractor HSE manager, and project director immediately
Notify Dubai Municipality and Ministry of Human Resources within 24 hours (UAE legal requirement)
Provide colleagues with immediate psychological first aid support
Secure all PTW, toolbox talk records, training records, and CCTV footage from the day
Photograph and video the scene in full detail before anything is disturbed
Document the exact position of the fall victim and any nearby equipment
Inspect and photograph the guardrail fixing points to determine when and how it was removed
Retrieve the worker's safety harness from the tool room — check its last inspection date
Collect: Permit to Work records for Level 7 work, toolbox talk attendance sheets for the past 7 days, safety induction records, training certificates for working at height
Interview at least 4 witnesses independently — do not allow group interviews
Obtain statements from the crew that removed the guardrail

content.text: The unsafe acts and unsafe conditions that directly caused the injury. These are what you 'see' at the scene.

rows: Worker not wearing safety harness — violated site PPE rule
Working at open edge without a safety anchor point
Guardrail removed from working platform and not reinstated
No temporary edge protection installed after guardrail removal
No supervisor present at the work location

content.text: The failures in the management system that allowed the unsafe acts and conditions to exist. These are the 'why' behind immediate causes.

rows: Inadequate supervision — supervisor managing 3 crews simultaneously
No procedure for temporary removal and reinstatement of guardrails
No such procedure in site safety plan
Worker not trained in working at height (Level 7 = >2m)
No Permit to Work issued for formwork installation at this level
PTW register had no active permit for Level 7
PPE inspection system absent — harnesses not checked in 3 months
No pre-task risk assessment (JSA) conducted before starting work
JSA form not completed for that day's activity

content.text: The fundamental failures in the organisation's safety management system that created the conditions for underlying and immediate causes to exist.

rows: Production pressure culture — deadline pressure caused supervisors to skip safety checks
Project manager emails instructing 'no delays' sent 3 days prior
Safety policy not embedded — fall protection policy existed on paper but not enforced
Policy document vs observed practice gap identified
Competency assessment absent — workers assigned to height work without verified competency
HR records show no competency verification process
Absent HSE monitoring — HSE manager had not visited Level 7 in 14 days
No near-miss reporting culture — 3 previous near-misses on the same level not reported
Workers disclosed in interviews, no formal reports found
Suspend ALL work at height across the entire site pending audit
Reinstate ALL guardrails before any height work resumes
100% harness-wear audit — any non-compliance = immediate stop-work
Notify regulatory authority and submit preliminary incident report
Retrain all workers on working at height requirements and PTW
Issue a mandatory guardrail removal/reinstatement procedure
Reduce supervisor span of control — 1 supervisor per crew maximum
Conduct comprehensive WAH audit of all levels with documented sign-off
Implement behavioural safety observation program with near-miss reporting
Install CCTV monitoring covering all elevated working platforms
Add competency verification to worker deployment process

content.text: Falls from height are the single largest cause of construction fatalities in the Gulf region. This case demonstrates that even when fall protection policies exist in documents, without active supervision, enforcement, and a culture that empowers workers to refuse unsafe work, written policies alone cannot prevent tragedy.

The removal of a guardrail by a previous crew without any procedure for authorisation, temporary replacement, or reinstatement was the most critical physical failure. Every site must have a documented guardrail removal procedure and that procedure must be known by all supervisors.

NEBOSH IG1 Element 9 connection: This incident maps directly to the 'Work Equipment' element, specifically the requirements for edge protection, working at height hierarchy (eliminate > collective protection > individual protection), and the absolute requirement for a safe system of work including PTW for height activities above 2 metres.

In the UAE, fatal construction incidents must be reported to Dubai Municipality or Abu Dhabi OHS within 24 hours. Saudi Arabia requires notification to MHRSD within 24 hours of a fatal incident. Qatar (under QCS 2014 Section 17) mandates scaffold inspection registers and a documented working at height plan for every project. Contractor companies found negligent in fatality investigations can face project suspension, financial penalties, and blacklisting from government contracts.
